## Git guide

### Step 1

Before beginning, a new project is created in RStudio. All files related to the project are stored within the same project folder to ensure reproducibility.

Within the RStudio project, a new Quarto document (.qmd file) is created. This file is saved in the same folder as the .Rproj file.

To render a .qmd file as an HTML document, the output format is specified in the YAML header at the top of the file by setting format: html. This instructs Quarto to generate an HTML file when the document is rendered. The resulting file is saved as example.html in the same folder as the source .qmd file.

The YAML header is defined as follows:

title: "example"  
author: "Thunchanok Udomittipong"  
format: html

### Step 2

To initialise the folder as a Git repository, a remote repository is first created on the GitHub website. In this case, the repository is named assignment-2. 
Next, the local project is initialised as a Git repository using the terminal with the following commands:

**git init**  
This command initialises Git tracking in the local project folder.

**git remote add origin git\@github.com:Thunchanok19/assignment-2.git**  
This connects the local repository to the remote GitHub repository. The repository URL is obtained from the GitHub interface by clicking the Code button and selecting the SSH option.  
Also, note that you may need to restart RStudio for Git to update.

**git add .**  
This command adds all file changes to the staging area.

**git commit -m "Initialise assignment-2 folder and add example.qmd file"**  
This command creates a commit with a descriptive message explaining the changes.

**git push origin main**
This command pushes all commits to the remote GitHub repository.
